Coordinated terrorist attacks in Paris perpetrated by the Islamic State killed 130 people and injured 413 others.

In Dietrich v The Queen, the High Court of Australia ruled that, although there is no absolute right to have publicly funded counsel, a judge should grant any request for an adjournment or stay in most circumstances in which an accused is unrepresented.
A single sugar-cube-sized portion of neutron star matter weighs approximately 1 billion tons—as much as Mount Everest.
Nerve impulses in the human peripheral nervous system can travel at speeds exceeding 400 kilometers per hour (250 mph).
Over 90% of Earth’s habitable living space exists within the deep oceans, where sunlight completely vanishes beyond 200 meters down.
The volcano Nevado del Ruiz (pictured) erupted, causing a volcanic mudslide that buried the town of Armero, Colombia, killing approximately 23,000 people.
South Korean boxer Kim Duk-koo suffered fatal brain injuries during a match with American Ray Mancini in Las Vegas, leading to significant rule changes in the sport.
Modern atomic clocks lose less than one second every 300 million years by measuring quantum state transitions of strontium atoms.
All human mitochondrial DNA is inherited almost exclusively through the maternal line, tracing back to a common ancestral maternal lineage.
Point Nemo in the South Pacific is so isolated from land that the closest human beings are often the astronauts on the International Space Station.
Six members of the DeFeo family were murdered in their home (house pictured) in Amityville, New York, events that later inspired the book The Amityville Horror and a subsequent media franchise.
Arab–Israeli conflict: In response to a Fatah landmine incident, the Israeli military conducted a large cross-border assault on the Jordanian-controlled West Bank village of Samu.
A man wielding a dagger was subdued as he was about to attack Sanzō Nosaka, the chairman of the Japanese Communist Party.
FC Dynamo Moscow opened their exhibition tour of the United Kingdom with a 3–3 draw against Chelsea, breaking the attendance record for a British club football match.
Walt Disney's Fantasia, the first commercial film shown with stereophonic sound, premiered at the Broadway Theatre in New York City.
The Holland Tunnel opened, connecting Manhattan with Jersey City under the Hudson River.
Zaian War: Zaian Berber tribesmen routed French forces at the Battle of El Herri in Morocco.

Octopuses possess 3 hearts, copper-based blue blood, and 9 brains. Approximately two-thirds of their 500 million neurons reside in their arms, allowing each arm to independently taste, explore, and manipulate objects without consulting the central brain.

Corvids (crows and ravens) remember individual human faces for decades. When a human treats a crow aggressively, the crow transmits that person’s description to the entire flock and teaches subsequent generations to identify and mob that specific human.

The peacock mantis shrimp punches with the acceleration of a .22 caliber bullet (80 km/h in water). The strike generates low-pressure cavitation bubbles that instantly collapse with temperatures exceeding 4,000°C—nearly as hot as the surface of the sun—emitting visible light flashes.

The immortal jellyfish (Turritopsis dohrnii) can cheat death entirely. When physically damaged, starved, or aged, it triggers cellular transdifferentiation—transforming its specialized cells back into early-stage polyps and rebooting its life cycle anew indefinitely.

The axolotl salamander can regrow lost limbs, crushed spines, and parts of its heart, retina, and brain without scar tissue. Transplanted organs from other axolotls are accepted without any immune rejection.

The Alaskan wood frog survives sub-zero winters by freezing 70% of its body water solid. Its heart completely stops beating and brain activity ceases for months, thawed unharmed when spring arrives via high-concentration glucose antifreeze.

Bumblebees build up positive electric charges as they fly. Because flowers possess a slight negative charge, pollen grains literally jump through the air onto the bee’s body, and the altered electric field signals to arriving bees that the flower was recently visited.

A blue whale’s main aorta is over 9 inches in diameter—large enough for a toddler to crawl through. Its heart weighs approximately 400 pounds (the size of a small golf cart), and its heartbeat can be detected by acoustic sensors over two miles away underwater.
